newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains prices move mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains prices move mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Grains futures prices were mixed on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Tuesday and dealers said turnover would only pick up when final details of this year's wheat harvest reach the market later this month.
"Many traders are on holiday, there is little activity on the market," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
Total grains futures turnover dropped to a meagre 425 contracts or 179.3 million forints from Monday's 644 lots or 375.2 million forints.
Feed wheat futures dropped the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne to 17,730 forints for September and 20,750 for March.
Monostori said feed wheat prices dropped in response to news that over 70 percent of the wheat had been harvested and on reaffirmed estimates of a five million tonnes wheat crop.
Untraded feed barley went limit-up for all but the May maturity which rose 100 forints.
"According to market talk barley is hard to get on the physical market," Monostori said. "On the other hand, this is an illiquid market and sudden price movements can happen".
Milling wheat prices were directionless on a lack of new information on the harvest.
"Everybody is just guessing now," Monostori said.
September milling wheat was steady, October rose 200 forints, November went up 20 and December dropped 150 forints in token turnover.

Euro wheat rose 400 forints for August 1998 and September 1998 to settle at 23,550 and 24,400 forints respectively. Monostori said euro wheat, introduced last Friday, was likely to take over the leading role from milling wheat in the longer term.
